newsitem.title: JAPAN: JVC plans DVD player with high-quality audio.
newsitem.headline: JVC plans DVD player with high-quality audio.

text.p: Victor Co of Japan said on Friday its digital video disc (DVD) player, scheduled for launch early this year, would seek to differentiate itself from competing models by offering high-quality audio.

"In order to make our product stand out from competitors, we have focused on high-quality sound, as the company, after all, originally started out as a record company," said a senior company official.
DVD is a new recording system which features large storage capacity and is touted as a next-generation replacement for videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs.
In November 1996, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co and Toshiba Corp launched the world's first DVD players.
A JVC spokesman said on Friday that his company would begin selling DVD players in Japan and the United States "very soon."
In November 1996, Victor launched three software titles for DVD players through its subsidiary Victor Entertainment Co.
A Victor spokesman said his company planned to introduce additional sofware titles, although he gave no further details.
Analysts have said the success of the new entertainment device will depend on whether manufacturers can offer a wide variety of attractive software titles.
